From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank model evaluation & next steps

Hi Rebecca —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of the call:
- Primary goal: improve search result relevance & CTR for product search (rerank stage).
- Key constraints: tail latency requirement < 120ms P95 for 95% of queries, and no regressions to CTR for top-1.
- Current baseline: your in-house model (baseline) runs at ~95ms P95, NDCG@10 0.42, MRR 0.57 on the sample eval set we reviewed.

What we delivered after the call (attached):
- acme_rerank_eval_results_q2.pdf — full eval table (NDCG/MRR by bucket, latency, token counts).
- acme_prompt_set_v3.csv — the prompt & query variants we used for the eval (edge cases + international variants).

Initial recommendation (high level):
- Candidate models: redwood/rerank-v2 (quantized q4f), and an L2-optimized variant (llama2-rerank-q4) as a cost-sensitive fallback.
- Expected lift: redwood/rerank-v2 shows +14% NDCG@10 and +9% MRR relative to your baseline on the held-out eval split. Latency for rerank-v2 measured at 110ms P95 on our standard N1 GPU profile (with batching disabled for tail measurements).

Proposed A/B plan (short):
- Phase 1 (staging smoke): run rerank-v2 on a shadow feed against 5k queries (~48 hours) to validate logging and parse edge cases.
- Phase 2 (live A/B): 10% traffic treatment, 4-week run, monitor NDCG@10, MRR, CTR (top1), end-to-end tail latency, and error rates.
- Rollback: automatic fallback to baseline on any regression > 2% absolute in top-1 CTR or a 20% spike in errors.

Next steps for you:
1) Share read-only access to the eval dataset (or an export) so we can re-run the exact split and guarantee parity on sampling.
2) Confirm that a 10% A/B is acceptable and the dates you prefer for a 4-week window.
3) Let us know any internal SLOs we must not violate (other than the tail latency you mentioned).

I attached the PDF + prompt set; I also added a summary doc to the shared Drive (link below). Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk through the eval table.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0149

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the artifacts. A few quick clarifying questions before we sign off on the 10% A/B: 

1) Latency: you mentioned 110ms P95 for rerank-v2 — is that including network hop + model inference or just inference on the GPU? We need to understand our real SLA impact.
2) Cost delta: can you provide an estimated cost per 10k queries for rerank-v2 vs our baseline?
3) Edge cases: will the prompt_set_v3 cover our international queries? There were a handful of QA examples in row 1–3 of our sample that historically trip models (abbreviated queries with emojis).

Also looping in EngOps (CC’d) — we’ll need a short runbook for rollback and for log collection (where should we send logs).

If you can confirm those three items, we can proceed with sharing the eval export and sign the A/B window.

— Rebecca
Head of Search, Acme AI
rebecca@acme.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rerank model evaluation & next steps

Hi Rebecca — thanks, great questions. Answers below and an operational plan.

1) Latency: the 110ms P95 number is model-side inference measured in our lab (includes tokenize+forward+postprocess) running on a single N1 GPU profile. Network hop and your ingress latency vary by region; in our internal runs you'd expect an E2E bump of ~6–15ms depending on carrier. For live tests we recommend adding a small buffer to your client-side SLO (we can instrument from your staging region to get an exact number).

2) Cost estimate (approx): rerank-v2 (q4f) ~ $0.85 per 10k queries; llama2-rerank-q4 fallback ~ $0.55 per 10k. Baseline (your current infra) is approximately $0.60 per 10k on your reported utilization. We'll provide detailed pricing for committed Dedicated capacity if you prefer.

3) Edge cases & prompt_set_v3: the CSV contains the international variants and emoji-trimmed queries — we flagged the top 120 edge cases with a "needs-attention" tag. I recommend we run the shadow feed (Phase 1) and review those flagged cases within 48 hours. If you want, we can add custom prompt templating for emoji-stripping as part of the preprocessor.

Operational A/B plan (expanded):
- Pre-run (2 business days): staging shadow feed against sample export to confirm logging hooks / schema. We will deliver a small smoke report (pass/fail on schema + 10 sample mismatches).
- Live A/B: 10% treatment, 4 weeks; primary signal: NDCG@10 (stat sig at p<0.05), secondary signals: MRR, top-1 CTR, latency P95, error rate.
- Monitoring & alerts: Redwood will push daily aggregated metrics to the shared Drive folder and send an alert to your EngOps webhook on any rollback trigger.
- Rollout cadence: ramp to 10% over 1 day (2/3/5 allocation), monitor first 24h closely.

Deliverables we’ll provide to you this week: 
- A reproducible eval run (notebook + CLI) to re-generate NDCG/MRR numbers (link below).
- A draft A/B runbook and rollback playbook (Doc in Drive).
- Full cost delta calc for 10k/100k/1M queries.

Links: 
- Eval notebook: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcD-example-acme-rerank
- A/B plan doc: https://docs.redwood.com/rerank/ndcg-mrr-ab-plan

If that works I’ll schedule the staging shadow run for Thursday and you can share the eval export (read-only) to rerank-eval@redwood.com.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: acme_rerank_eval_results_q2.pdf (same as earlier)
